pages.en:
I lay out a futon in the living room and put the unconscious Illya to bed.

Despite having fainted, she looks peaceful in her sleep. There seems to be nothing wrong with her.
pages.mirrorMoon:
I lay a futon down in the living room and place Illya on it.
Even though she’s unconscious, Illya’s face looks calm and there doesn’t seem to be anything wrong with her.

pages.en:
“Ow…! Tohsaka, what kind of person hits someone who's already injured!?”

“Be quiet. I'm going to the trouble of treating you, so sit still for once.

“Now raise your right arm. You probably don't need it anymore, but I'll put some medicine on this side too, just in case.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Ow…! Tohsaka, that’s no way to treat a wounded guy!”
“Shut up. I’m treating your wounds, so be quiet for a while.
Here, raise your right hand. I don’t think it’s necessary, but I’ll put some medicine on it as well.”

pages.en:
“——That's cold.”

“If you can feel it, you're fine. Now for the bandage.”

She deftly winds it around me from the right shoulder down.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Tchit’s cold.”
“It’s fine if you can feel. Here, we’ll wrap this up next.”
She skillfully wraps the bandage around my right shoulder.

キャスターとの一件の後、居間に戻るなり遠坂は俺の傷の治療を始めた。
始めたのだが、傷はもう大部分が塞がっており、あとは形だけの処置を施すだけだった。

pages.en:
It is after ten o'clock.

The instant we returned to the living room after the incident with Caster, Tohsaka began treating my wounds.

Or tried to. Most of them had already closed, leaving her with little more than the formality of dressing them.
pages.mirrorMoon:
It’s past ten.
After returning to the living room, Tohsaka started to treat my wounds.
She started, but the wounds have mostly already healed, so all that’s left is to treat them just for show.

貴方、本当に人間？」
……なんか、似たようなコトを前にも言わなかったか、おまえ。

pages.en:
“There, finished. Honestly, your body makes no sense. Vampires are about the only things with healing powers on that level.

“Are you certain you're human?”

…Haven't you said something very much like that before?
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Done. But you sure do have a strange body. Only vampires have bodies with such healing powers.
Are you really human?”
…I think she asked me something similar a while ago.

pages.ja:
「あのな、オレはまっとうな人間だよ。
オレだってどうしてこんななのか知らないんだから、訊かれたって判るもんか」
pages.jaRuby:
「あのな、オレはまっとうな人間だよ。

pages.en:
“Listen, I'm an entirely ordinary human being.

“I don't know why my body does this either, so how am I supposed to answer when you ask me?”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Hey, I’m a normal human being.
I don’t even know how this is happening, so I can’t give you an answer.”

pages.ja:
「冗談、まっとうな人間が脊髄切られてピンシャンしてるかっていうのよ。
便利だからあえて追及しなかったけど、いい加減不気味になってきたわ。もしかしてアンタ、首を切られないかぎり死なない土地の出だったりしない？」

pages.en:
“Don't be ridiculous. Ordinary humans don't spring back to their feet after having their spinal cords severed.

“I left the matter alone because it was useful, but it's beginning to disturb me. You weren't born in some land where people can't die unless their heads are cut off, were you?”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Don’t play with me. Would a normal human be up and running after they’ve had their spinal cord cut?
I never asked because it was useful, but it’s getting too freaky now. Maybe you’re from some place where people can only be killed by decapitation?”

pages.ja:
「………………」
何が厄介かって、遠坂がわりと本気で疑っているのが恐ろしい。
こやつ、いつか手斧を持って俺の首を狙ってくるやもしれぬ。

pages.en:
“………………”

The worst part is that Tohsaka appears to be entertaining the suspicion in earnest.

One day, this woman may come after my neck with a hand axe.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“……”
The worst part is, Tohsaka is seriously considering that.
She might come after my neck one day with an axe in hand.

pages.ja:

pages.mirrorMoon:
“Hey, don’t you think so too, Saber?
I think you’re the cause, but it’s still too far beyond human.”

pages.en: “What…? Does Shirou's healing ability not belong to Shirou himself?”
pages.mirrorMoon: “Huh…? Shirou’s healing power is not his own?”

pages.en:
“?”

“?”

Tohsaka and I exchange involuntary glances.

Something about Saber has been wrong for some time now.

…No, I know when it began.

Ever since that golden knight appeared, some part of Saber's customary spirit has deserted her.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…?”
“…?”
Tohsaka and I look at each other.
Saber’s acting strange.
…No, I know why.
Saber’s spirit has been low since that golden knight appeared.

“…Well, we'll set Shirou aside for now.

pages.mirrorMoon:
“…Well, let’s put the matter of Shirou on hold.
More importantly, Saber, did you know that gold guy? He was saying you were his.”

遠坂の問いは、そのまま俺の問いでもある。

pages.en:
“………………”

Saber does not answer.

It could hardly be clearer that the matter is difficult for her to discuss.

Even so, I want the answer.

Tohsaka's question is mine as well.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“……”
Saber doesn’t answer.
It’s obviously something she doesn’t want to talk about.
But I still want to know.
Tohsaka’s question is mine as well.

“A Servant—so he really is one.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…Yes. I do not wish to admit it, but I do know him. But it is impossible. There are only seven Servants. He cannot be summoned.”

That much was obvious at a glance.

But if it is true, we have a serious problem.
pages.mirrorMoon:
No, that’s obvious.
But in that case, there’s a big problem.

pages.mirrorMoon: “He is of class Archer. Of course, he is not the Archer whom Rin made a contract with. His abilities and character are too different.”

pages.ja:

pages.jaRuby:

…I understand that too.

I saw him for only a moment, but that was more than enough to feel what kind of monster he was.
pages.mirrorMoon:
…I know that too.
It only lasted a short while, but I was able to feel how much of a monster he was.

pages.en:
“Wait. That doesn't make sense.

“If he is an Archer-class Servant, that makes eight.

“Seven is supposed to be the absolute limit within a single cycle. The Grail never summons replacements simply because the numbers fall. It doesn't possess enough magical energy to summon more than seven in the first place.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Hold on. That’s not right.
If he’s the Servant Archer, that makes eight.
Seven should be the limit of the summons in a single period. It’s not like they restock when some of them disappear. After all, even the Holy Grail doesn’t have the magical energy to summon more than seven.”

って、待った。

Saber fought in a sea of fire…?

“”

…Why should that surprise me now?

Father Kotomine already told me that the great fire was caused by the Holy Grail War.

Then I have no reason to be shocked.

After all—I have been unconsciously doing everything I can to avoid considering it.

…It’s nothing new.
Kotomine already told me that the fire was caused by the Holy Grail War.
So this shouldn’t be a surprise.
It’s justI was unconsciously trying not to think about it until now.

pages.en:
“…Kiritsugu killed every feeling within himself, and he killed every enemy before him.

“I do not know what he believed in so fiercely that he would go so far. I know only that when the Grail—the object of all his struggle—stood before him, he ordered me to destroy it.

“…To speak honestly:

“Never have I cursed the existence of the Command Spells, or the one who betrayed me, more bitterly than I did in that moment.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…Kiritsugu killed every emotion and killed every enemy.
I do not know what he believed in to make him do so, but he ordered me to destroy the Holy Grail when it was in front of him.
To be honest…
I have never cursed the Command Spell or a Master who has betrayed me, more than I did at that time.”

pages.en:
When I think about it, I knew nothing of Kiritsugu before the day he found me ten years ago.

I had no means of learning what sort of man he had been before then—and no need to know.

Even if Kiritsugu Emiya had once been merciless, it would change nothing.

The man who took Shirou Emiya home had been as foolishly childish as anyone could be.

For me, that alone is the truth.
pages.mirrorMoon:
Come to think of it, I don’t know what Kiritsugu was like before that time ten years ago.
I couldn’t guess anything about him before that time, and I saw no need to learn about such things.
It doesn’t change a thing even if Kiritsugu was cold-hearted.
The man that adopted me was really childlike.
So my memory is my only truth.
